A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, table, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C–D report original linear-model experiments and deep-network evaluations, including corruption robustness and augmentation-alignment results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental outcomes in Table 1 and Figures 2–10, including linear-model simulations and image-classification experiments.

M1.justification: The reconstruction and joint-embedding objectives, model families, and augmentation procedures are retained. The revised reconstruction formula corrects the theoretical analysis of the existing objective without introducing a new training or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, Kuzushiji-MNIST, single-cell RNA-seq, ImageNet-100, and CIFAR-10 under the same corruption scenarios. New discussion of language and video does not introduce evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BYOL, DINO, and MAE. Appendix D retains SimCLR versus supervised learning and the SimCLR, BYOL, and VICReg augmentation-alignment experiments; the linear-model comparator set is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendices C–D retain the PCA and noise construction, corruption/alignment sweeps, linear-probing metrics, architectures, and training schedules. The clean and corrupted test-set evaluations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The sample-size/noise/alignment analyses, supervised-versus-SSL robustness comparison, augmentation-noise experiments, and representation visualizations are retained. The new paradigm schematic supplies no additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1.2 still specifies five random seeds, and the heatmap captions still describe averages over five seeds. Error bars and shaded uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and all matched experimental plots retain their values and trends. For example, Gaussian-noise severity-5 accuracy remains 59.0% for DINO and 44.8% for MAE. Appendix heatmap entries also match.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.1 receive a localized mathematical correction: augmentation means replace original inputs where required in the moment matrices and reconstruction derivation. Equation (13) now uses DE E[tau(x_i)], removing the implicit mean-preservation assumption. The joint-embedding theorem and alignment propositions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about closed-form solutions, augmentation alignment, supervised-learning consistency, and the relative advantages of reconstruction versus joint embedding at different noise magnitudes.

C2.justification: Section 1.1 adds a substantive language-versus-vision explanation based on semantic compression and low-level variability. Section 3 adds discussion of nonlinear feature maps and wide-network relevance. Existing experimental interpretations and the intertwined-signal/noise limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain the same preprocessing instructions, backbones, optimizers, hyperparameters, schedules, and lightly-library defaults. No new implementation or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on V-JEPA, BERT, language semantics, and wide-network linearization, while removing Bordes et al. and DINOv2 citations. These changes broaden supporting context without redefining the main novelty claim.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites and expands introductory explanations and divides them into Sections 1.1–1.3. It also edits section titles, wording, cross-references, affiliations, and conference text; the overall main-text and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 1, a schematic comparing reconstruction and joint-embedding pipelines. Existing Figures 1–9 become Figures 2–10 with limited caption edits and page reflow; their experimental displays and Table 1's structure are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical correctness by incorporating augmentation means into Theorem 3.1 and its proof, addressing an implicit restriction in v1. The new schematic and expanded introduction improve accessibility and contextual explanation. These are useful, bounded gains; the principal alignment results and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
